thread:
maria: ok team — we need a pragmatic plan to carve out the policy-evaluator and the hot-cache layer from the monolith. this has been a recurring tech debt drag and makes routing/batching hacks messy.
alex: agree. what's the minimal boundary we can cut that gives isolation without 6 months of churn?
jia: can we extract read-only cache first? i.e., introduce a cache sidecar that serves prefix/KV reads while writes still go to monolith. low-risk.
sam: +1. that lets us move caching heuristics out of runtime. also gives us a place to attach telemetry for cache hit patterns.
maria: proposed phases (very lightweight):
1) cache sidecar (read-only) with a stable gRPC iface.
2) promote sidecar to writable cache and add async writeback.
3) extract policy-evaluator as its own service referencing the cache via the new iface.
4) route-by-policy and deprecate in-process logic.
alex: timeline wise, phase 1 could be a 3-week spike + 2-week rollout. we should plan for a dark-launch window of 2 weeks.
jia: what about data ownership? the canonical source of truth remains the monolith for now. sidecar maintains a local LRU and a backing sync to monolith.
sam: we need migration scripts for cache materialization for warm start. also a migration plan for policy rules (versioned config).
maria: rollout policy sketch:
- deploy sidecar to 10% of hosts with header-based routing: "X-Cache-Mode: sidecar" for canary.
- run in read-only mode for 2 weeks while recording diffs.
- enable writeback behind a flag, small percentage, monitor.
- cutover when hit-stability and correctness thresholds met.
alex: sample header for canary test:

curl -H "X-Cache-Mode: sidecar" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

jia: telemetry we need: per-route hit-rate, error-rate, observed latency delta, policy-eval decisions count. add tracing span names: cache.sidecar.fetch and policy.evaluator.eval.
sam: ops concerns: need a fallback path in runtime if sidecar times out. 150ms soft timeout then fallback to in-process call. add circuit-breaker.
maria: risks:
- drift between monolith rules and extracted policy-evaluator -> mitigate with versioned configs and diff alerts.
- cold-start cache causing latency spikes -> mitigate with pre-warm job and sampling throttles.
- coupling through DB migrations -> minimize schema changes; prefer feature-flags for schema reads.
alex: do we need a migration ticket for infra and k8s resources? i can open one with resource estimates.
sam: i'll draft the SLO change proposal for the 90/99 latency windows during the rollout.
deploy-bot: created ticket ARCH-8722 for "policy-evaluator & sidecar cache extraction: infra resources" assigned to @alex.
maria: next steps: alex open infra ticket, jia prototype sidecar API (3-day spike), sam start SLO doc, i'll write the RFC addendum with the phased plan. keep the thread updated.
alex: will do, starting ticket now.
jia: prototyping tomorrow. will post notes.
sam: SLO draft by end of week.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
